principle: National uncertainty is calibrated on strict chronological errors of the selected point model and must not reuse territorial residuals or current-only political judgement.

calibration_history.rule: For a target fold, use only selected-model residual transitions whose target year is at or before that fold's origin year.

scale_rule.transition_energy: sqrt(mean_j(e_tj^2)) over the nine frozen buckets
scale_rule.prospective_scale: maximum transition energy among chronologically available prior residuals
scale_rule.reason: A monotone worst-observed national-shock floor avoids unstable party covariance estimation from only a handful of independent elections and allows a shock to migrate to a different party.

draw_rule.tangent_constraint: Draw a common multivariate Student-t innovation in the sum-zero simplex tangent space. The Gaussian precursor is centered across the nine components and scaled by sqrt(8/9) so each raw component has the frozen scalar t scale.
draw_rule.simplex_recovery: Euclidean projection of point_share + innovation onto the non-negative unit simplex.
draw_rule.cross_party_covariance: No fitted 9x9 covariance; exchangeable tangent dependence only (sum-to-zero implies negative off-diagonal dependence).

coverage_gate.pooled_unit: 36 party-fold component observations across the four scored folds

limitations: Only five historical national transitions are available including the training transition; tail probabilities are therefore structurally uncertain.
The spherical tangent rule deliberately sacrifices party-specific precision rather than infer a fragile covariance matrix from n<<p.
A PASS means historical interval coverage is adequate under the frozen diagnostic; it does not guarantee 2026 calibration.
